claims.text: The author has three active companies, sgit.ai, the SGit Newsroom and RiskMandate, and none of them has a LinkedIn page.
claims.quote: I now have three active companies, sgit.ai, the SGit Newsroom and RiskMandate, and none of them has a LinkedIn page.

claims.text: The drafts are published before the pages exist, because the site documents the story of what is happening, including the parts a founder usually does in private.
claims.quote: Here it is before it is done.

claims.text: Requested without logging in on 18 October 2026, the addresses sgit-ai, riskmandate and sgit-newsroom under linkedin.com/company all returned 404, as did the obvious variants.
claims.quote: all returned 404, as did the obvious variants

claims.text: LinkedIn's showcase pages do not share followers with the parent, appear in search only for existing followers, cannot have jobs, and nobody can list one as their employer.
claims.quote: They do not share followers with the parent, appear in search only for people who already follow them, cannot have jobs, and nobody can list one as their employer.

claims.text: The newsroom gets a company page rather than a showcase page, because it is now a business of its own with its own model.
claims.quote: The newsroom is now a business of its own, with its own model, so it gets a company page.

claims.text: The Cyber Boardroom Limited is the commercial vehicle behind sgit.ai and RiskMandate; the three new pages list each other as affiliated and The Cyber Boardroom's page stays as the entity.
claims.quote: The three new pages list each other as affiliated, and The Cyber Boardroom's page stays as the entity.

claims.text: LinkedIn asks for a logo of at least 268 by 268 pixels, and a page newsletter needs more than 150 followers.
claims.quote: A page newsletter needs more than 150 followers

claims.text: The tagline limit of 120 characters and the about limit of 2,000 are from LinkedIn Learning, not a help page; the headline's 220 and the profile about's 2,600 are from third-party guides.
claims.quote: are from LinkedIn Learning, not a help page

claims.text: The sgit.ai tagline is 117 of 120 characters: Git for encrypted vaults, for people and AI agents; files encrypted on your machine, servers see only ciphertext.
claims.quote: Git for encrypted vaults, for people and AI agents. Files are encrypted on your machine; servers see only ciphertext.

claims.text: sgit's three parts, the command line, SG/Vault in the browser and SG/Send, are open source under Apache 2.0; the code is free and the running service is sold through sgraph.ai.
claims.quote: The code is free; the running, maintained service is what we sell, through sgraph.ai.

claims.text: sgit is in beta with no compliance certification yet, and everything claimed about it is written down, versioned and testable, including more than fifty published vaults with their read keys.
claims.quote: more than fifty published vaults with their read keys

value.unit: published vaults with read keys (more than)

claims.text: Thirty first posts are drafted, ten per page, every one an article or page already published on the sites.
claims.quote: Ten per page, each an article or page on the sites.

claims.text: The six newsletter issues so far are already on LinkedIn in Deterministic GenAI; once the page has more than 150 followers it can carry its own.
claims.quote: once the page has more than 150 followers it can carry its own

claims.text: The newsroom's about page draft counts more than 180 articles since 17 August 2026, four wires in beta and a newsletter.
claims.quote: More than 180 articles since 17 August 2026, four wires in beta (industry, OWASP, AWS and Portugal), and a newsletter.

claims.text: The newsroom is a working model of how news could be paid for: readers pay for the share of a page they actually read, after reading, and their rating sets the price.
claims.quote: Readers pay for the share of a page they actually read, after they have read it, and their rating sets the price.

claims.text: The newsroom's content is CC BY 4.0 and its code Apache 2.0, and it is published by the sgit project, which builds the stack it writes about and says so on every page.
claims.quote: Published by the sgit project, which builds the stack it writes about; we say so on every page.

claims.text: RiskMandate is co-founded, so its page is agreed with the co-founder before it goes up, and the drafts use only what riskmandate.ai says publicly.
claims.quote: RiskMandate is co-founded, and its page is agreed with my co-founder before it goes up.

claims.text: An ABP is a record for one agent in one deployment in four parts: its reach, its mandate, the gap between them, and the barriers; it carries no score.
claims.quote: An ABP is a record for one agent in one deployment, in four parts

claims.text: RiskMandate stays out of the request path on purpose; enforcement happens in the tools and platforms the agent runs on, and the ABP says what should be enforced and records what is.
claims.quote: We stay out of the request path on purpose.

claims.text: RiskMandate's pricing is one-time per agent per deployment, from a £10 pack to £1,500 with a signing professional; sixteen ABP templates are free and the vocabulary is open at abp.sgit.ai under CC BY 4.0.
claims.quote: Sixteen ABP templates are free, and the vocabulary is open at abp.sgit.ai under CC BY 4.0.

claims.text: RiskMandate is not an insurer; its aim is to make agentic AI insurable.
claims.quote: RiskMandate is not an insurer. Its aim is to make agentic AI insurable.

claims.text: The profile's about opens with building the tools AI agents need before they can be trusted with real work, and writing about it in the open.
claims.quote: I build the tools I think AI agents need before we can trust them with real work, and I write about it in the open.

claims.text: The author spent around thirty years in security in the UK, was on the OWASP Board, created the OWASP O2 Platform and organised the OWASP Summits in Lisbon in 2011 and Woburn in 2017.
claims.quote: I was on the OWASP Board, created the OWASP O2 Platform, and organised the OWASP Summits in Lisbon in 2011 and Woburn in 2017.

claims.text: The author has written ten books on Leanpub, on security, DevSecOps and developers.
claims.quote: I have written ten books on Leanpub, on security, DevSecOps and developers.

claims.text: None of the pages exists yet; these are drafts.
claims.quote: None of the pages exists yet. These are drafts.

claims.text: A free address is not proof that no page exists under another address.
claims.quote: A free address is not proof that no page exists under another address.

claims.text: Some limits are not from LinkedIn's help pages but from LinkedIn Learning, blogs and guides, and should be checked in the editor.
claims.quote: Some limits are not from LinkedIn's help pages.

claims.text: The founding years and locations are not on the sites; the drafts say London, from the author's GitHub profile.
claims.quote: The drafts say London, from my GitHub profile.

claims.text: RiskMandate's text is not final until it is agreed with the co-founder.
claims.quote: RiskMandate's text is not final until it is agreed with my co-founder.

claims.text: The article comes from a voice memo of 18 October 2026, with LinkedIn's help pages read that day by a research agent and the companies' own sites.
claims.quote: LinkedIn's help pages, read that day by a research agent
